title: Plans — round 9: the question box, and the last things you haven't signed off

steps.path: A paused plan, after pressing Ask the assistant
steps.headline: Ask the assistant opens a small box where you can type a question, or leave it blank.
steps.changed: Pressing Ask shows a box with Cancel and Send. What you type goes to the assistant with the plan's details.
steps.notice: You can ask something specific, as the beta tester expected.

steps.path: The chat after sending a question
steps.headline: The chat shows what you asked.
steps.changed: The line reads "You asked the assistant about this plan: …" with your words, or just the first part if you left the box empty.
steps.notice: Your question stays visible in the conversation.

steps.path: A plan paused because a specialist was cut off while running a command
steps.headline: Only when a cut-off action may have reached outside your computer does the card ask you, and it warns Continue may repeat it.
steps.changed: Cut-off reads and file edits now recover on their own. A command, web request or connected app still pauses, with "Continue may run it again. Check first whether it already happened." plus Ask the assistant.
steps.notice: You're only interrupted when repeating an action could matter.
steps.risk: The warning still shows when the command was harmless to repeat.

steps.path: Repeating steps that used all their rounds
steps.headline: A plan whose repeated steps never met their goal offers Ask the assistant and Stop.
steps.changed: Continue and Add budget aren't offered because neither would help; the assistant can suggest a revised plan if you ask.
steps.notice: One click to get advice on what to do next.

steps.path: A plan paused at its limit, with too small an amount typed
steps.headline: Add budget starts at the smallest amount that lets the plan finish, and refuses less.
steps.changed: The line "Add at least 12,500 tokens to continue." turns red below the minimum and Continue is disabled. Continue adds the budget and restarts the plan in one press.
steps.notice: Adding budget can't leave the plan stuck.
steps.risk: The minimum can be larger than you expect, because it also covers restarting the specialist.

steps.path: A plan button the app refused
steps.headline: A refused plan button shows the app's standard error with Retry.
steps.changed: You asked when this happens: when the plan is running in another YouCoded window, it changed a moment before your click, its model or price changed since you saw it, the app is still starting, or its saved file can't be read.
steps.notice: Errors here look and work like everywhere else.

steps.path: After pressing Comment and sending a note
steps.headline: Your comment appears in the chat with a short plain note asking for a revised plan.
steps.changed: The line after your note reads "(Feedback on your plan: please revise it and propose it again.)"; the assistant is also told, out of sight, to answer with a new plan card.

steps.path: Specialists popup while a plan's specialist is asking you something
steps.headline: A plan with a waiting question is listed under Needs you and opens by itself.
steps.changed: The plan's card shows "1 needs you" and is already open to the specialist's question with Yes and No.

steps.headline: Is it fine that pausing is free but continuing re-sends each unfinished specialist's instructions?
steps.today: A paused plan uses nothing while it waits. When you press Continue, each specialist that hadn't finished starts again from what it saved, which means sending its instructions again; that counts toward the plan's budget.
steps.problem: You asked whether pausing and resuming costs anything. The card doesn't say.
steps.proposal: Leave it, or add a short line on paused cards.

options.label: Leave it as is
pros: The limit already includes the restart cost.
cons: You don't see why the minimum Add budget can be larger than expected.

options.label: Add a short line
pros: Explains the restart cost up front.
cons: One more line on every paused card.
